# Overview

In May 2046, an anomalous post appeared on SaidIt, an internal social forum used by employees of Tenant Thread, a property management company. The post is done under the name of John Windward on 4.21 am local time. The post is in gibberish and found in a forum that appears random. The challenge is to:

-   investigate how this happened and create a visual tool to describes the sequence of events that led up to the post
    -   detailed view on the exact chain of events for this message of interest
    -   system overview that contextualizes the message chain in the overall system
-   Understanding the post: what it mean and origin of their contents
-   concerning behaviours that could repeat
    -   determine prior incidents 
    -   propose system intervention to prevent it happening again

## Data

The challenge dataset consists of two files: `MC2_Data.json`, which records system activity events, and `org_chart.json`, which describes the organisational structure of Tenant Thread. A key feature of the event log is the `parties` field, which may reference people, agents, or systems. This suggests employees are assisted by autonomous agents capable of acting on their behalf, meaning not all recorded actions are directly initiated by the employee.

## Analytical Approach

1.  Identify the anomalous post and establish its structural anomalies
2.  Understand the organisational context used including where John Windward sits within Tenant Thread
3.  Immediate chain of events leading to the post traced backwards step by step
4.  Full interaction network is mapped to establish a basline of normal behavior
5.  Investigate origin and content of post
6.  Characterize the propagation loop that carried the malicious instructions
7.  Examine why John is the one who posted and not others
8.  Discover and compare prior incidents following the same pattern
9.  Propose data-backed intervention

::: callout-note
### Key Finding: Interpreting SaidIt Event Types

Inspection of the event log reveals two distinct SaidIT-related event types.

-   `saidit_post` events are associated with a person account and typically contain a valid `details.poster_id` and `details.timestamp`.
-   `post_saidit` events are associated with an agent interacting with the SaidIT system and do not contain these fields.

This distinction suggests that `saidit_post` represents a completed forum post made by a user themselves, whereas `post_saidit` records agent-system interactions involved in the posting process.
:::

The challenge states the post appeared under John Windward's name at 4:21am local time. To determine whether John was responsible for the activity, all events involving him on May 17 are examined.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
  arrange(datetime) %>%

         details.content, details.forum, details.poster_id,
```

## Label Node

Next is to tag each agent as "Normal only", "Loop only" or "Both". This will tell us the distribution of the agents.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
loop_nodes <- unique(c(loop_edges$sender, 
                       loop_edges$receiver))
normal_nodes <- unique(c(normal_edges$sender,
                         normal_edges$receiver))
all_nodes <- union(loop_nodes, 
                   normal_nodes)
 
node_meta <- tibble(id = all_nodes) %>%
  mutate(
    in_loop = id %in% loop_nodes,
    in_normal = id %in% normal_nodes,
    node_role = case_when(
      in_loop & in_normal ~ "Both",
      in_loop & !in_normal ~ "Loop only",
      TRUE ~ "Normal only"
    ),
    label_highlight = case_when(
      id == "john_windward" ~ "John Windward\n(posted)",
      id == "emma_harbor" ~ "Emma Harbor\n(SwiftWren origin)",
      id == "gabriel_sonar" ~ "Gabriel Sonar\n(loop origin)",
      TRUE ~ str_replace_all(id, "_", " ")
    )
  )
 
node_meta %>%
  count(node_role, name = "n_agents") %>%
```

The second prevention is to do cross-department checks. The SwiftWren propagation events shows that the propagation occurred crossed department boundaries. By doing checks, it will flag `queue_subordinate_task` events that violate the organisation hierarchy which can be done by using `org_edges`.

```{.r .cell-code}
  org_edges %>%
    filter(relation == "contains",
           str_detect(target, "^person:")) %>%
    mutate(
      person = str_remove(target, "person:"),
      dept   = str_remove(source, "department:|team:")

    select(person, dept)

  filter(relation == "contains",
         str_detect(source, "^department:"),

    dept = str_remove(source, "department:")
```
